title: GPU heap surge causing tenant cascade and cache ghosting — emergency remediation and runtime patch
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Multiple customers in Hosted and Dedicated tiers reported burst GPU OOMs over the past 48 hours, correlated with an increase in long-lived prefix cache growth for a small set of tenants. Symptoms included high per-tenant GPU allocation, slow eviction, and stale cache entries that were not reclaimed leading to severe memory fragmentation and subsequent OOMs. Hosts entered repeated OOM-restart cycles causing degraded throughput and elevated tail latency.

What happened: At ~2026-03-10T02:10 UTC we received a sev2 escalation from a high-usage customer in US-WEST. Within two hours we observed similar spikes across a handful of dedicated pools and a subset of hosted nodes. The runtime's eviction fast-path failed to free metadata for certain cache entries under a specific race (evict pointer moved before tombstone write completed), leaving ghost entries in the slab allocator. Over many allocations this produced slab starvation and high external fragmentation in the GPU memory arena. When large generation requests landed they failed to satisfy contiguous allocation requests and triggered GPU OOMs.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Enabled request-level throttling for affected customers via the rate-limiter to reduce allocation pressure (temporary).
- Disabled aggressive prefix caching for tenants matching the spike pattern via console feature flag (console: feature/disable-prefix-cache-tenant).
- Triggered controlled rolling restarts of 32 affected nodes with an emergency reclaim agent to compact slab arenas on startup.
- Deployed a hotpatch (runtime:hotfix/734215-throttle-evict-order) that changes eviction ordering to prefer tombstone completion before pointer advancement to stop creating new ghost entries.
- Increased Dedicated pool headroom by 15% to reduce immediate OOM surface.

Root cause hypothesis: A narrow race in the prefix cache eviction code allowed the eviction pointer to advance before tombstone/state persisted to the KV index in some high-concurrency code paths. The allocator's free fast-path did not coalesce certain slab fragments when metadata was removed out-of-order, catalyzing fragmentation. The combination of long-lived cache entries (multi-hour sessions) and bursts of large sequence-length requests pushed fragmented arenas past the threshold causing allocation failures.

Data & evidence:
- Grafana alert: grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/alerts?panel=oom-spike-734215
- Incident timeline and traces: http://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/traces?query=ENG-734215
- Heap snapshot and slab fragment histogram stored at s3://redwood-incidents/ENG-734215/heapshots/
- Pager duty timeline and customer escalations compiled in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-734215+Incident+Report
- Emergency PR with hotpatch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2048

Proposed permanent fix plan:
1) Runtime allocator change: implement a coalescing fast-path that is resilient to out-of-order tombstone removal and ensures contiguous free spans are merged on free; add unit + fuzz tests. (owner: Rohit)
2) KV index compaction: background compactor that converts stale tombstones into reclaimed metadata on a controlled cadence. Add metrics for tombstone count and compaction throughput. (owner: Mei Chen)
3) Eviction ordering: formalize eviction commit ordering in the prefix cache to guarantee tombstone persist before pointer advance. Add deterministic linearizability tests. (owner: SRE team)
4) Router backpressure: introduce a soft-queueing mechanism to shed or queue large-sequence requests when per-tenant allocation growth exceeds a threshold. (owner: Jordan Lee)
5) Observability: add slab fragmentation heatmap, per-tenant allocation delta metric, and automated alerts for tombstone backlog. (owner: Observability)
updates: 2026-03-10 02:14 - Pager: Multiple 5xx and OOM alerts from US-WEST dedicated pools. On-call responded and added initial triage notes.
2026-03-10 03:02 - Investigation: Heap and slab histograms show a rising concentration of small free fragments and a plateau in total free memory. Patterns match a slab fragmentation pathology.
2026-03-10 05:10 - Mitigation: Rolled out rate-limiter throttle for 6 customers and disabled prefix-cache for 3 suspected tenants; immediate reduction in OOM frequency observed.
2026-03-10 08:45 - Hotpatch deployed: runtime:hotfix/734215-throttle-evict-order (PR #2048). Patch prevents new ghost entries; nodes show no new tombstone growth after deploy.
2026-03-11 11:00 - Rollout: Executed controlled rolling restart of 32 nodes with reclaim agent; post-restart fragmentation improved by ~42% in sampled nodes (see S3 heapshots).

2026-03-12 09:30 - Customer comms: Sent interim incident update to impacted customers and provided ETA for permanent fix. Link to communications: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1IncidentComms734215
2026-03-13 14:20 - PR open: Runtime allocator coalesce RFC and prototype branch created (github:runtime/pulls/2055). Awaiting review from allocator core team.
2026-03-14 10:05 - Post-mitigation: No repeat OOM cascades in the last 36 hours; still tracking tombstone backlog and memory fragmentation metrics during peak traffic windows.
